subject: Qualification: PoC deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification: PoC deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp

Thanks again for the call earlier today — appreciate the time, Alex and Priya. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the PoC approach.

Summary from discovery:
- Primary goal: evaluate inference economics and latency at 99th percentile for Acme's customer-facing summarization flow (~1k tokens per request, 8 qps peak).
- Security/regulatory: customer data must remain in US-only regions and log retention requirements for audit (7 years) may push toward Dedicated or Private options.
- Success metrics (prelim): 99th percentile latency < 300ms for 1k-token requests, sustained throughput >= 8 qps, request cost <= $0.02/request (TBD after profiling).
- Stakeholders: Alex (Product), Priya (Platform/Infra), Procurement (TBD).

PoC options we discussed:
1) Hosted API (fastest to start): Redwood-hosted with regional routing and strict access controls. Pros: quick onboarding, lower operational overhead. Cons: less control over dedicated capacity and data residency guarantees beyond region contract.
2) Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU pool in a US region for predictable throughput and data isolation. Pros: predictable latency/costs, supports higher scale. Cons: longer lead time to provision, requires commitment.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): Full customer-managed deployment; maximum control for compliance. Pros: meets strict data governance, isolated control plane. Cons: longest setup, more ops overhead.

Proposed PoC plan (attached: Acme_PoC_Draft_v1.pdf):
- Duration: 4 weeks (2-week profiling & tuning, 2-week load run & validation)
- Week 0: Kickoff + infra prep (networking, credential exchange, sizing decision)
- Week 1-2: Profiling with representative corpus, kernel/quantization recommendations, initial cost/latency baseline
- Week 3-4: Full-run validation against success metrics + final recommendations and runbook

Immediate asks:
- Confirm preferred deployment mode to surface any procurement lead times (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Confirm technical contact and availability for a kickoff next week (Priya?)
- Procurement/finance contact for potential PO or MSA review.

I attached a draft PoC plan and a capacity-sizing sheet. Happy to adjust timelines based on your procurement and platform constraints.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

- Can Dedicated be provisioned in our preferred us-west-2 region and support reserved capacity for a 4-week PoC?
- Rough ballpark on incremental monthly cost for the small dedicated pool vs hosted (we'll need this for budgeting).
- Priya is looped in as our infra lead — she'll own the technical kickoff.

I'll introduce Procurement separately (they need an estimated SOW / cost to start an internal approval).

Great — Dedicated makes sense for those constraints. Answers to your questions below and next steps: 

- Region & provisioning: yes, we can provision a dedicated pool in us-west-2. For a "small" PoC pool (2 x A100-equivalent nodes with burst to 4 when required) we can typically provision in ~7 business days depending on capacity; if you need guaranteed timing we can surface that as an SLA addendum for the trial.
- Ballpark cost: for the 4-week PoC we can offer a trial rate of $X,XXX/week (will provide a precise quote via procurement). For comparison, Hosted unit costs are lower per-token but without the guaranteed isolation.
- Success metrics and instrumentation: we'll instrument request tracing and token-level cost analytics, and share a dashboard with per-route latency percentiles.

Updated PoC milestones (attached updated plan):
- Sizing confirmation & procurement (Day -7 to Day 0)
- Technical kickoff & infra handshake (Day 0)
- Profiling & tuning (Day 1–14)
- Load validation & acceptance (Day 15–28)

3) Any additional compliance docs we should prepare (SOC 2 evidence, data flow diagrams, etc.)

I'll loop in Marissa from our Solutions team to help with the kickoff and to own the runbook deliverables.
